To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the readiness potential, contingent negative variation, and vertex positive wave are all reliable and useful indices of the neural events underlying perception.
the RP and CNV reflect common neural mechanisms when both are studied during a complex psychological situation.
the CNV is a reliable index of expectancy, and that the RP is a reliable index, not of expectancy, but rather of the neural events leading to the perception of stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the relationship between brain potentials and psychological processes.

the relationship between the readiness potential (RP) of Libet et al. (1979, 1983) and the contingent negative variation (CNC) of Walter et al. (1964) in the context of an experiment where subjects are asked to perceive a brief visual stimulus and then to report their perceptions on the basis of a cue.
the study of the relationship between the brain and the behavior of a person.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RP is a reliable index of neural processes preceding correct or incorrect perception, and that P302 is not.

the RP is a reliable index of a neural process associated with a decision to perform an action and that this process may be related to a number of different behavioral events, depending on the experimental situation in which the RP occurs.
the CNV is not a reliable index of expectancy or attention, and that it is not possible to separate the RP and the P302 on the basis of their behavioral correlations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CNV is a reliable index of motivational/expectancy/ attention factors, and the RP is a reliable index both of the motivational/expectancy/factor and the neural events associated specifically with correct or incorrect perception of the stimulus.

the RP is a reliable and valid index of the neural activity associated with the preparation for the execution of a voluntary motor response, whereas the CNV is a valid index of the motivational state associated with the expectancy of a stimulus.
the RP is an index of the readiness to perform a task (in this case, to perceive) and the CNV an index of expectancy and/or motivation to report.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the readiness potential, vertex positive and contingent negative variation can be reliably recorded in a situation involving a complex cognitive task.
the CNV and RP are not independent measures of neural processes but are related.
the CNV is not a simple reflection of expectancy but rather a more global index of the subject’s state of readiness.
